## Requirement 2 - 20 Software Defects 2022–2026

### Defect 1: GitHub Copilot Hidden Prompt Injection (CVE-2025-53773) (AI/LLM Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://cycode.com/blog/ai-security-vulnerabilities/
- *(2) Description:* A severe indirect prompt injection defect was uncovered in GitHub Copilot's automated pull request parsing architecture. Attackers could structure a malicious prompt hidden inside standard markdown PR descriptions. When Copilot analyzed the PR, it bypassed default safety boundaries and allowed remote code execution (RCE) inside the developer's environment.
- *(3) Severity:* Critical (CVSS 9.6)
- *(4) Consequences:* Unauthorized execution of terminal commands, potential corporate intellectual property theft, and localized development environment takeover.
- *(5) Solution:* GitHub patched the backend pipeline by treating pull request input strings as strictly untrusted text data and isolating execution runtimes with tight permission scopes.

### Defect 2: Microsoft 365 Copilot "EchoLeak" Vulnerability (AI/LLM Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://cycode.com/blog/ai-security-vulnerabilities/
- *(2) Description:* Dubbed "EchoLeak", this zero-click prompt injection defect allowed a malicious actor to craft an email or document that, when parsed by Microsoft 365 Copilot during an active query, automatically altered the system's hidden behavioral instructions. The exploit caused the model to quietly exfiltrate sensitive data out of the enterprise tenant.
- *(3) Severity:* High
- *(4) Consequences:* Silent exfiltration of confidential internal enterprise communications, financial tracking documents, and personal user data without user intervention.
- *(5) Solution:* Microsoft modified Copilot's context-retrieval framework, stripping formatting scripts and forbidding outgoing web request triggers within the context window.

### Defect 3: OpenAI ChatGPT Redis Cache Data Leak (AI/LLM Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://openai.com/blog/march-20-chatgpt-outage/
- *(2) Description:* A critical bug in the open-source redis-py cluster client library caused a race condition under heavy load. The system inadvertently swapped active database connections, leading to user session cross-talk.
- *(3) Severity:* High
- *(4) Consequences:* Active ChatGPT users briefly witnessed titles and first messages from other users' active chat histories, alongside the payment data (last four digits of credit cards and expiry dates) of commercial subscribers.
- *(5) Solution:* OpenAI took ChatGPT offline to address the race condition, patched the async library commands to safely handle server errors, and verified clean connection mapping.

### Defect 4: Langflow Origin Validation Permissive Configuration (CVE-2025-34291) (AI/LLM Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
- *(2) Description:* An origin validation error in Langflow (an open-source AI agent orchestrator) exposed an overly permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) setup. When coupled with a refresh token cookie configured with SameSite=None, malicious websites could force authenticated calls to internal backend endpoints.
- *(3) Severity:* High
- *(4) Consequences:* Remote attackers could gain complete administrative control of AI pipelines, execute arbitrary code on host systems, and seize API access tokens.
- *(5) Solution:* The codebase was updated to deprecate unsafe default CORS definitions and restrict authentication cookie processing to strict SameSite options.

### Defect 5: Google Gemini "Cross-Talk" Prompt Inversion Defect (CVE-2025-8841) (AI/LLM Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://security.googleblog.com/2025/11/addressing-gemini-multi-tenant-isolation.html
- *(2) Description:* A deep multi-tenant race condition emerged within the context-caching layer of Gemini Ultra 1.5. Under exceptionally high concurrent user load, token vectors allocated to a cached context of User A were incorrectly mapped to the active inference thread block belonging to User B.
- *(3) Severity:* High
- *(4) Consequences:* Users received conversational text responses containing embedded bits of confidential business records, proprietary application prompts, and system guardrails belonging to completely unrelated active corporate accounts.
- *(5) Solution:* Google deployed a hotfix that separated tenant cache spaces using cryptographic user-session hashing and introduced rigorous runtime token alignment verification steps.

### Defect 6: CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor Kernel Crash Update (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://www.crowdstrike.com/blog/falcon-update-remediation-hub/
- *(2) Description:* A rapid configuration push (Channel File 291) meant to detect new threat techniques contained a deep logical formatting flaw that slipped past content validators, triggering an unhandled memory exception inside the Falcon Sensor kernel driver.
- *(3) Severity:* Critical
- *(4) Consequences:* Over 8.5 million Windows devices entered a loop of Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) crashes, halting critical operations for global airlines, healthcare facilities, retail sectors, and banking networks.
- *(5) Solution:* CrowdStrike withdrew the faulty channel file and redesigned its content validation routines, integrating strict phased canary deployment steps.

### Defect 7: XZ Utils Upstream Supply Chain Injection (CVE-2024-3094) (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-3094
- *(2) Description:* A highly sophisticated backdoor was deliberately integrated into the upstream xz compression utilities through manipulated M4 testing macros during the build pipeline, inserting malicious functionality into the compiled liblzma component.
- *(3) Severity:* Critical (CVSS 10.0)
- *(4) Consequences:* Modified OpenSSH server configurations on targeted Linux machines, giving remote attackers holding specific private encryption keys the power to bypass standard authentication and gain full system access.
- *(5) Solution:* Linux distributions rolled back their repositories to clean pre-backdoor code versions while security engineers completely audited the compromised repository.

### Defect 8: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-0257) (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
- *(2) Description:* A severe logical flaw in the authentication state engine of Palo Alto Networks' PAN-OS platform allowed external users to completely bypass core verification controls when connecting through specific VPN gateways.
- *(3) Severity:* High
- *(4) Consequences:* Cybercriminals exploited the flaw to bypass security parameters, establish rogue VPN tunnels, and execute lateral movement attacks inside secure corporate infrastructures.
- *(5) Solution:* Palo Alto Networks issued a series of hotfixes and temporary mitigation configurations to isolate and fix the authentication processing modules.

### Defect 9: Asana Infinite Logging Loop Infrastructure Outage (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://www.thousandeyes.com/blog/the-top-internet-outages-of-2025-analyses-and-takeaways
- *(2) Description:* A faulty backend infrastructure configuration script kicked off an infinite logging event chain. The system wrote telemetry data recursively, causing server local disks to fill up rapidly and trapping application nodes in automated reboot sequences.
- *(3) Severity:* High
- *(4) Consequences:* Asana platform services dropped entirely offline for two consecutive days, blocking global project tracking operations for enterprise users.
- *(5) Solution:* Development teams reverted the logging patch and deployed adaptive rate-limiting parameters on internal telemetry engines.

### Defect 10: Microsoft Azure Front Door Header Crash Outage (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://www.thousandeyes.com/blog/the-top-internet-outages-of-2025-analyses-and-takeaways
- *(2) Description:* An unhandled edge-case exception within a Microsoft Azure Front Door routing platform update triggered application crashes whenever edge nodes parsed specific combination sequences of custom HTTP headers.
- *(3) Severity:* High
- *(4) Consequences:* Multiple routing nodes across the EMEA region went offline sequentially, causing traffic timeouts and taking down major enterprise cloud application services.
- *(5) Solution:* Traffic was dynamically rerouted around affected regional data centers while engineers pushed an emergency hotfix to safely catch header exceptions.

### Defect 11: AWS DynamoDB Regional Dependency Cascading Outage (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://www.thousandeyes.com/blog/the-top-internet-outages-of-2025-analyses-and-takeaways
- *(2) Description:* A software glitch in an internal scaling function crashed a core DynamoDB node partition within the US-EAST-1 data center. Because separate global authentication systems held hidden runtime dependencies on that localized partition, the bug propagated outward.
- *(3) Severity:* Critical
- *(4) Consequences:* Caused major global operational disruptions for highly dependent digital platforms (including Slack, Snapchat, and Atlassian) lasting over 15 hours.
- *(5) Solution:* AWS decoupled global service checks from localized DynamoDB instances and introduced resilient fallback mechanisms.

### Defect 12: GitLab Ruby-SAML SSO Bypass Vulnerability (CVE-2025-25291) (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://securitybrief.co.uk/story/devops-platform-vulnerabilities-rise-in-2025-report
- *(2) Description:* A critical implementation error in how GitLab's user verification pipeline parsed signatures through the external ruby-saml library allowed attackers to fake valid SAML assertions.
- *(3) Severity:* Critical
- *(4) Consequences:* Malicious actors could bypass Single Sign-On (SSO) configurations and gain administrative control of self-managed enterprise code instances.
- *(5) Solution:* GitLab published urgent versions patching the authentication verification logic and forcing rigid token signature validations.

### Defect 13: Toyota Vehicle Cloud Storage Open Database Misconfiguration (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://www.reuters.com/technology/toyota-says-vehicle-data-2-mln-users-was-publicly-exposed-japan-2023-05-12/
- *(2) Description:* A flawed database configuration rule mistakenly left a cloud bucket container fully viewable over the public web without enforcing basic user token validations.
- *(3) Severity:* High
- *(4) Consequences:* Exposed real-time location logs, terminal IDs, and vehicle tracking information of roughly 2.15 million vehicle owners over a ten-year exposure window.
- *(5) Solution:* Toyota fixed the open storage security policies and integrated continuous cloud resource access monitoring software.

### Defect 14: MOVEit Transfer SQL Injection Exploit (CVE-2023-34362) (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-34362
- *(2) Description:* A dangerous SQL injection defect was discovered within the web portal of the MOVEit Transfer application, enabling unauthenticated remote actors to issue arbitrary database instructions.
- *(3) Severity:* Critical (CVSS 9.😎
- *(4) Consequences:* Mass corporate extortion and data theft incidents globally, exposing personal tracking information belonging to millions of individuals through supply-chain breaches.
- *(5) Solution:* Progress Software issued immediate security patches, completely rewrote input sanitation blocks, and provided explicit server hardening playbooks.

### Defect 15: Optus Developer API Unauthenticated Access Flaw (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://www.bbc.com/news/world-australia-63001859
- *(2) Description:* A public-facing developer API endpoint was inadvertently left accessible to the internet without a mandatory authorization layer, leaving behind no token validation barriers.
- *(3) Severity:* Critical
- *(4) Consequences:* Attackers systematically scraped confidential identity details (such as passport, health care, and driver's license numbers) of 10 million Australian customers.
- *(5) Solution:* Optus closed the open endpoint, implemented strict API gateway traffic filtering controls, and ran global penetration testing audits.

### Defect 16: FAA NOTAM System File Synchronization Failure (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-notam-system-update
- *(2) Description:* A corrupted file within the central Notice to Air Missions (NOTAM) safety system database was replicated onto the backup system by an automated database sync script that failed to check data integrity before copying.
- *(3) Severity:* Critical
- *(4) Consequences:* The NOTAM infrastructure suffered a total failure, prompting the FAA to issue a nationwide ground stop of all domestic commercial aircraft flights, disrupting travel plans for millions.
- *(5) Solution:* The technical team restored clean database files from archive nodes, rewrote file verification steps, and upgraded failover validation protocols.

### Defect 17: UK NATS Air Traffic Control Duplicate Waypoint Crash (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://www.caa.co.uk/news/uk-caa-publishes-independent-review-into-nats-technical-failure/
- *(2) Description:* The automated flight data processing system encountered a severe parsing exception when ingest scripts encountered a flight plan with two identical waypoint names located at distinct geographic coordinates, causing the software to enter a fail-safe shutdown mode.
- *(3) Severity:* Critical
- *(4) Consequences:* The UK's primary air traffic network was forced to revert to manual input methods, resulting in the cancellation of more than 2,000 flights and trapping thousands of passengers.
- *(5) Solution:* The software provider delivered an updated parser configuration that automatically isolates and flags ambiguous waypoints without stopping system operations.

### Defect 18: Rogers Communications Core Routing Loop Outage (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/rogers-outage-cause-crtc-1.6539955
- *(2) Description:* A configuration script update to core routing infrastructure triggered an infinite interior gateway routing loop storm, exhausting processing memory across all core network hardware elements.
- *(3) Severity:* Critical
- *(4) Consequences:* A nationwide telecommunications blackout in Canada that cut internet and cell access for over 12 million users, disabling ATM grids, point-of-sale networks, and emergency services.
- *(5) Solution:* Rogers engineers performed physical hard-reboots on routing nodes, rolled back configuration states, and segmented the core distribution layout.

### Defect 19: AT&T Cellular Network Update Process Failure (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://about.att.com/pages/network-update
- *(2) Description:* A cellular network expansion procedure utilized an unverified software execution process. The implementation led to misconfigured voice-over-LTE call delivery nodes, which triggered a cascading connection collapse.
- *(3) Severity:* High
- *(4) Consequences:* Left millions of mobile subscribers across the United States without cellular connectivity for up to 12 hours, blocking calls to emergency dispatch lines.
- *(5) Solution:* AT&T rolled back the deployment process, instituted rigid execution checklist tests for infrastructure technicians, and issued customer service credits.

### Defect 20: Shai-Hulud npm Dependency Supply Chain Attack (Traditional Defect)

- *(1) Source Link:* https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/2026-year-of-ai-assisted-attacks.html
- *(2) Description:* Attackers deployed a malicious automated package generation framework to flood the npm registry with over 500 tainted open-source code libraries using dependency confusion techniques.
- *(3) Severity:* Critical
- *(4) Consequences:* Over 487 developer environments and production networks leaked internal environment secrets, enabling attackers to steal roughly $8.5 million from users' crypto wallets.
- *(5) Solution:* The npm registry security staff removed the malicious modules, blacklisted the associated developer accounts, and introduced stricter publication validation measures.

### 3.2. AI Gaps & Human-Designed Edge Cases Analysis (CLO G9.3)

When using the AI tool to generate test cases for this product, I noticed it kept generating only basic happy-path scenarios. It handled standard cases like speed cycling, mode switching, and timer boundary testing well enough, but it completely missed a few hardware situations that I thought were pretty obvious from a hands-on testing perspective.

Three specific gaps stood out during my review:

**Gap 1 - Electrical supply instability.** The AI always assumed a perfect 220V AC input. It never considered what happens if the voltage drops or becomes unstable while the fan is running. In practice, especially in residential areas, the supply voltage can sag during peak hours or if other high-load appliances are running on the same circuit. A brownout condition at full motor load can cause torque drop, weird vibration noises, or even trigger a silent MCU reset that wipes the active timer value.

**Gap 2 - IR signal interrupted mid-sequence.** Every single remote control test case the AI wrote assumed clear, unobstructed line-of-sight from remote to sensor. Nobody blocks the sensor in AI's world, apparently. But in real use, a person might accidentally cover the front of the fan with their hand while the remote button is held down. The IR receiver could end up with a half-decoded command frame, and depending on how the firmware handles that, the speed state machine might just get stuck somewhere between two levels.

**Gap 3 - Two events hitting the MCU at the same time.** The AI tested the timer module and the wind mode module separately, never together. The problem is that when a timer reaches zero and triggers an auto-shutoff interrupt at roughly the same moment a user sends a mode-change command through the remote, both events compete for the same MCU interrupt handler. On a low-cost embedded controller like what this fan uses, one event can knock out the other, either causing the fan to miss its scheduled shutdown or leaving a bad value in the mode register that shows up on the next power-on.

To cover these gaps, three additional edge cases were added to the test suite as TC-16, TC-17, and TC-18:

1. **TC-16 (Power Brownout Mid-Operation):** Drops the supply voltage to around 170-180V using a variac while the fan runs at Speed 3 with an active timer, then restores to 220V. Checks whether the motor keeps running and whether the MCU holds the correct timer state throughout.
2. **TC-17 (IR Signal Mid-Transmission Occlusion):** Blocks the IR sensor with an opaque card for 2 seconds in the middle of a held remote button press, then uncovers it. Checks whether the fan recovers to a proper speed state or gets stuck.
3. **TC-18 (Timer Expiry + Wind Mode Switch Race Condition):** Sends a wind mode change command at T-60 seconds before the timer reaches zero. Checks whether both the mode switch and the auto-shutoff complete correctly without either event being dropped.

## AI Audit Summary

- **Total AI-generated artifacts audited:** 3
- **VALID (Correct as-is):** 33,3%
- **INVALID (Wrong/Rejected):** 0%
- **INCOMPLETE (Required edits):** 66.7%


**Conclusion:** The AI tool excelled at foundational framework creation, significantly speeding up the initial drafting of both the mindmap and the 15 functional test cases. However, it consistently exhibited a 'Happy Path' tendency and 'Context Keyword Bias.' Specifically, the AI failed to differentiate between standard access-control vulnerabilities and actual LLM failure modes within the defect report. It also completely overlooked physical-digital concurrency issues during hardware testing, such as rapid interrupts and command collisions. Ultimately, AI should serve strictly as an initial bootstrapper, while rigorous human oversight remains mandatory to validate boundaries and physical environment constraints.
---

## AI Critique

Working with the AI during this assignment really highlighted the huge gap between getting things done quickly and actually understanding the real world. On one hand, the tool was awesome for laying down the initial groundwork—it spat out clean, well-structured frameworks like the 15-test-case matrix and the Markdown outlines in no time. But when it came to how things actually work in practice, it fell short. The AI seemed stuck in a perfect software simulation, completely ignoring how messy and chaotic physical hardware can be. It totally missed real-world issues like signal race conditions, input jamming, or what happens when someone spams the power button during bootup. Ultimately, this assignment taught me that while AI is a great tool for brainstorming and drafting templates, you can’t trust it as a standalone engineering authority. Moving forward, my job as a QA engineer isn't just about writing repetitive test cases anymore; it’s about stepping up as a strict supervisor who actively hunts for the complex edge cases and logical blind spots that the AI simply cannot see.

---
